newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Electronics re-rating heads Singapore share deals.
newsitem.headline: Electronics re-rating heads Singapore share deals.

text.p: Electronics stocks led the way in early trade on the Singapore stock exchange on Monday with the sector seemingly undergoing a re-rating process, dealers said.
"It seems the electronics sector will be leading the Singapore economy around again and that's giving rise to a re-rating," a dealer with a local institution said.
An electronics bias was obvious in early dealing with the Stock Exchange of Singapore electronics index rising 2.45 points to 160.14.
The Straits Times Industrials Index slipped 9.72 points to 1971.24 by 0230 GMT. One dealer said blue chips were suffering because "foreign buyers are still concerned about the regional currencies".
Venture Manufacturing was an early electronics surger, hitting a new high of Singapore $8.00 before settling back to S$7.30 by 0230 GMT, up S$0.45 on Friday's close.
Gul Technologies was also active, with four million shares traded in the first 90 minutes. The stock rose S$0.025 to S$0.950.
Conglomerate Keppel Corp was the fastest early mover with 6.1 million shares traded, but the stock remained unchanged at S$6.50.
Blue chips Cycle & Carriage and Fraser & Neave saw falls of S$0.30 each to S$12.60 and S$10.30 respectively.
